Confirmed value: Zero wages is not zero qualifying income
Details: The income alternative uses MAGI-based monthly household income, not just wages. California’s outreach letter says income from any source, and the enacted state statute (AB 2161) uses MAGI-based financial methods. Zero earned income alone is not an automatic disqualification.

If verified monthly MAGI-based household income reaches the federal threshold ($580 at the current $7.25 wage), this is an alternative to tracking 80 activity hours. Financial eligibility for Medi-Cal is a separate test. No personal eligibility determination is made here.

Topic: If qualifying income is below the threshold
Details: Community service, a qualifying work program, at least half-time education, combinations of qualifying hours, or a qualifying exclusion/exception can satisfy or remove the requirement.

Topic: If income is too high for Medi-Cal
Details: Apply through the state marketplace for an eligibility decision and plan options. Marketplace savings use expected annual household income; the Medicaid work rule is not a universal requirement to buy insurance.

Topic: Do not intentionally fail the rule
Details: DHCS warns that losing Medi-Cal for not meeting these rules prevents financial help for a Covered California plan. Full-price coverage may be necessary; do not assume subsidized coverage is the fallback.

Federal general deadline is January 1, 2027. The DHCS public work page says January 1, 2027; the MEDIL body says effective January 1, 2027; its enclosed member letter says March 2027. The enacted state statute says "no sooner than January 1, 2027" and only after DHCS confirms its systems are ready. Plan conservatively for January and rely on your county’s individual notices, not an assumed grace period.
Investment interest is counted; MAGI also adds tax-exempt interest. A bank balance and the interest it produces are not the same thing.

HealthCare.gov instructs use of net rental and royalty income, not gross rent receipts. The work-income alternative uses MAGI methodology (42 CFR 435.552(f)(2)). Do not treat every rent deposit as countable profit.
Capital gains are listed as income. This does not establish that each particular Kalshi contract is a capital asset or a section 1256 contract.

No Kalshi-specific IRS classification was verified. A targeted irs.gov search on 2026-10-19 found no event-contract or Kalshi guidance. Do not assume all contracts are futures eligible for section 1256 or a 60/40 split. General IRS trader guidance is context only, not confirmation for your contracts.

IRS Publication 550 describes securities/commodities trader gains as generally not subject to self-employment tax, with a dealer exception. This general tax rule does not decide Medicaid activity-hour eligibility or your Kalshi treatment.
Self-employment income is reported after business expenses. Separately paid property-management services and net rental income are different categories; no fee income is assumed for you.

CMS specifies monthly MAGI-based household income for the work-income route. Marketplace premium assistance instead estimates the coverage year’s annual household income. Do not use annual trading turnover as monthly income.
No dollar amounts, tax household, deductions, or contract records were supplied. Personal MAGI and eligibility cannot be confirmed. Unknown is not recorded as $0.

Confirmed value: $580 per month at current federal wage
Details: Threshold is federal minimum wage × 80, not California minimum wage. CMS requires MAGI-based household income. Income must also stay within applicable Medi-Cal financial eligibility rules.

The six-month average applies only to a seasonal worker as described in 26 U.S.C. 45R(d)(5)(B): "a worker who performs labor or services on a seasonal basis as defined by the Secretary of Labor". Both the enacted California statute and the federal regulation say so. Volatile trading or rental income does not by itself establish seasonal-worker status. The DHCS member letter’s broader wording is flagged at R55.

CMS includes paid, in-kind and unpaid work; federal rule discussion includes self-employment. Taxable earnings are not the only activity route. Whether your specific work qualifies remains unresolved.
CMS describes structured unpaid work benefiting the community under an established organization’s oversight, not partisan activity. It can be voluntary or court-mandated.
A qualifying program is defined by federal law; CMS includes certain state employment/training and veterans’ programs. Do not assume independent job searching qualifies.

School/institution determines enrollment status. CMS includes qualifying higher education, career/technical, high school and equivalency programs. A generic online course is not automatically sufficient. The DHCS member letter’s “part time” wording is flagged at R60.
Combine qualifying work, community service, work-program hours and less-than-half-time educational hours under CMS rules. Half-time education independently satisfies the route.

Confirmed value: Can count as work under the federal definition
Details: The federal rule defines work to include paid, in-kind and unpaid work, and its preamble names property managers paid in free or reduced rent and self-employed business owners as examples. This states the general rule only; whether your own hours are accepted is not confirmed (see R53).

No official California or CMS Kalshi-specific approval of personal trading hours was verified. The federal rule counts self-employment and "owning a business" as work, but no official source reviewed addresses own-account event-contract trading. Do not rely on “full-time trader” alone; the income route may be more directly supported if the threshold is met.
Section 71119 creates community engagement requirements; section 71107 establishes six-month redeterminations for the adult expansion group. This is not merely a proposal.
Issued June 1, published June 3, 2026; legal effective date July 31, 2026. General state implementation deadline January 1, 2027. Federal Register notes a June 29 correction.

Applies to the Medicaid adult group and certain section 1115 populations, subject to exclusions and exceptions. It is not a work mandate for everyone seeking healthcare. Your age and eligibility group are unknown.

CMS: certain applicants must demonstrate compliance for at least one month before application; current enrollees for one or more months between renewals. California’s enacted statute sets the months: for applicants, the one month immediately before the month of application; for enrollees, any one month between the last determination and the next scheduled redetermination. DHCS outreach says any month since last renewal. Do not infer every month must be documented.

If the state cannot verify compliance, it must notify the person and allow 30 calendar days to show compliance or exemption. In California the 30 days start on the date the notice is received (deemed 5 days after the date on the notice), coverage continues during that period, and the county must check every other basis of eligibility and offer a fair hearing before denying. Reapplication is allowed at any time.
DHCS outreach promises a written notice explaining what is needed before coverage ends and how to appeal a disputed decision. Open and respond to county notices promptly.

For some ACA expansion adults, with listed exceptions. DHCS’s public page says six-month checks start March 1, 2027; the member letter says "Beginning January 2027" and the MEDIL body says section 71107 is effective January 1, 2027. A work-rule exclusion does not automatically prove exemption from all renewal obligations.

Confirmed value: Children / older adults / other eligibility groups
Details: DHCS lists children 0–18 and adults 65+ outside work rules. CMS includes mandatory exceptions for other qualifying categorically needy groups and Medicare circumstances. This is not a personal finding.
DHCS includes pregnancy and one year after; CMS includes entitlement to postpartum medical assistance.

Confirmed value: Dependent child 13 or younger / disabled person
Details: CMS lists parents, guardians, caretaker relatives or family caregivers of a dependent child 13 or younger or a disabled individual, under defined conditions. California’s statute also lists caregivers of "an individual with a chronic or other health condition, disability, or functional limitation." Being a property manager is not itself a caregiving exclusion.

CMS includes medically frail people or special medical needs significantly impairing compliance; DHCS lists disability and serious physical/mental conditions or substance-use problems. Do not assume every diagnosis automatically qualifies.
CMS specifies a total disability rating; being a veteran alone is not the listed exclusion.

CMS lists American Indians/Alaska Natives and qualifying former foster youth. DHCS describes people under 26 who were in foster care on their 18th birthday; California’s statute lists "Foster youth or former foster youth under 26 years of age" and Indians, Urban Indians, California Indians and people eligible for the Indian Health Service.

CMS lists people meeting TANF work rules, household SNAP recipients subject to SNAP work rules, and participants in qualifying drug/alcohol treatment programs. California calls TANF CalWORKs and SNAP CalFresh; not every recipient is automatically covered.
CMS lists inmates; DHCS lists release within the last 90 days. These do not establish general Medicaid payment for services while incarcerated.

CMS allows specified inpatient/medical care, medical travel, disaster and high-unemployment exceptions. DHCS outreach lists these circumstances and promises additional county notices when applicable. No county-level exception is assumed here.

DHCS offers Medi-Cal applications through BenefitsCal, Covered California, mail, phone and in person. Its online estimator is not an eligibility decision. No enrollment or application is submitted by this site.

DHCS chart lists $22,025 annual income for a one-person household; 2026 monthly chart lists $1,836 at 138% FPL. These are reference figures, not a determination; your household size is unknown. Covered California’s 2027 chart says Medi-Cal uses the current year’s FPL, so do not carry these amounts forward as verified 2027 limits.

Covered California announced $300 million for state subsidies, compared with $190 million, and 2027 assistance up to 200% FPL ($31,920 individual). This is not a blanket replacement for Medi-Cal lost over work-rule noncompliance.

Covered California’s 2026 guide says the state subsidy requires eligibility for federal advance premium tax credits and the subsidized application. Do not assume state help bypasses the noncompliance restriction.

No general exemption based solely on zero earned income was identified. California’s statute lists the excluded individuals (§14005.69(b)(2)(A)-(N)), deemed-compliance categories ((f)(1)-(5)) and short-term hardships ((h)(1)-(4)); none is based on having no earned income. (f)(5) also covers "any other federally required or approved exemptions outlined in the state plan or waivers"; no zero-earned-income exemption of that kind was found. Use a documented income or activity route, or a qualifying exclusion.

Confirmed value: No property limit for MAGI Medi-Cal; non-MAGI limits apply
Details: DHCS lists "No property limits" for MAGI Medi-Cal (the adult group). Non-MAGI programs require proof of property such as bank accounts or rental homes and have limits: DHCS says the limit is $130,000 for one person through June 30, 2027 and $21,000 from July 1, 2027, for people 65+, people with disabilities, nursing-home residents and families over the federal-tax-rule income limit. Owning rentals does not alone decide MAGI eligibility; the income they produce does.

Confirmed value: Outreach, data-first verification and statutory protections
Details: DHCS says lawmakers invested in resources and promises information on paid or volunteer work, training and schools. The enacted statute requires DHCS to verify compliance through data interfaces (wage data, aid codes, claims and social-services data) and consent-based platforms. Counties must confirm conflicting data with you before any adverse action and consider every other basis of eligibility before denial. None of this is a waiver of the rule.

Recommended sequence: use the official application route to establish household, age/category and income eligibility. Do not report $0 total income solely because wages are zero. Applications require your authorization and accurate records.

Confirmed value: Suggested records, not a verified checklist
Details: Keep interest statements, net rental calculations, relevant tax records and trading reports organized by month. For self-employment, DHCS’s general application list asks for Schedule C and a profit-and-loss statement for the last three months, and allows self-attestation when there is no proof of income. Exact county documentation for the work rule is not confirmed.

Recommended decision sequence: assess counted income; review exclusions; if needed use a qualifying activity with reliable attendance/hour records. Specific acceptance of Kalshi or property-management logs remains unverified.

Confirmed value: Read notices / renew / appeal if needed
Details: DHCS recommends up-to-date contact details and BenefitsCal for documents, renewals and messages. Respond within deadlines and use the appeal instructions if a decision seems wrong.

DHCS directs people who do not qualify to Covered California to shop for health plans. Annual MAGI and other eligibility rules determine savings; work-rule denial may preclude financial help. No premium quote can be verified without personal details.

DHCS’s public changes page says "Work at a job and earn at least $580 a month". The September enclosure says income from any source; CMS specifies monthly MAGI-based household income; the enacted statute (AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(6)) uses MAGI-based financial methods for the individual’s MAGI-based household budget. This dashboard follows the statute and the CMS standard, but does not guarantee county acceptance of any specific financial record.

Topic: Your own property-management hours and records
Details: Not confirmed for you: whether your county accepts hours spent managing your own rentals, and what records it wants. The corrected federal rule says a state may not deny eligibility "solely because the individual is unable to produce documentation where none exists". Suggested preparation (a recommendation, not a requirement): a dated duty and hours log, leases and rent-credit agreements, and Schedule C/E records.

Amends Welfare and Institutions Code §14005.69. It requires the rule "no sooner than January 1, 2027" and only after DHCS confirms its systems are ready. It sets the look-back months, the MAGI-based income test and seasonal-worker-only averaging. It adds a 30-day cure period running from receipt of the notice and requires the county to check other bases of eligibility before denial. DHCS county guidance ACWDL 25-30 is labelled preliminary and predates it.

Confirmed value: Statute: seasonal workers only · member letter: “hours change frequently”
Details: The DHCS member letter (August 31, 2026) says people "whose hours change frequently or who have seasonal jobs" can average $580 over six months. The enacted statute (September 14, 2026), the federal regulation and DHCS’s own Medi-Cal Changes page limit averaging to seasonal workers ("Be a seasonal worker and earn an average of $580 a month"). Do not rely on averaging to cover months when trading or rental income is irregular.

Confirmed value: Data first; documentation required when reasonably available from 2028
Details: The state must check reliable information it already has before asking you. Before January 1, 2028 it may require documentation or accept other information. From January 1, 2028 it must require documentation whenever documentation is reasonably available. It must accept other information when none is available, and may not deny solely for missing documents that do not exist.

Confirmed value: From January 1, 2027: one month for adults without children
Details: DHCS says that starting January 1, 2027, Medi-Cal will pay one month of medical bills from before you applied for adults without children, and two months for everyone else. This is separate from the work rule. Today’s Help Center still describes the current three-month retroactive period.

Confirmed value: Covered California: previous year · Medi-Cal: current year
Details: Covered California’s 2027 chart says marketplace programs use the previous year’s FPL, while Medi-Cal uses the current year’s FPL as calculated by DHCS. It lists the California State Subsidy at 100%–200% FPL and says income above 400% FPL is not eligible for a federal premium tax credit. A 2027 DHCS Medi-Cal chart was not located.

DHCS’s Medi-Cal Changes page says copayments from October 1, 2028 apply to adults 19–64 who "Make more than $15,560 a year". DHCS’s own 2026 chart lists the one-person poverty guideline as $15,960. The two figures do not match, so no copayment threshold is stated here. Flagged for review.

Confirmed value: Statute and rule: at least half-time · member letter: “at least part time”
Details: The DHCS member letter says "Go to school at least part time". The enacted statute, the federal regulation and DHCS’s Medi-Cal Changes page all require enrollment at least half-time, with less-than-half-time hours counted only in combination with other activities. Rely on the half-time standard; the school decides your enrollment status.
